newsitem.title: UK: REED-ELS SEES FIVE PCT HIT IN 97 FROM STERLING.
newsitem.headline: REED-ELS SEES FIVE PCT HIT IN 97 FROM STERLING.

text.p: The current strength of sterling could depress the reported headline earnings of Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier by five percent if maintained throughout the year, co-chairman Nigel Stapleton said on Wednesday.

In a telephone interview, Stapleton said that current currency levels would drag down reported earnings for the Reed-Elsevier combined businesses by five percent. Those headline figures are expressed in sterling.

But he noted that although this has a negative effect on the the earnings per share of Reed International Plc , expressed in sterling, it has a correspondingly favourable effect on the guilder EPS of Elsevier NV .
"It's good news for Elsevier and bad for Reed," he said. "(But) the two share prices are linked so much that Elsevier should pull Reed up with it in some respects," Stapleton said.
"(But) the two share prices are linked so much that Elsevier should pull Reed up with it in some respects," Stapleton said.

Reed Elsevier's 1996 pre-tax profit rose 11 percent to 805 million pounds despite a four percent dilution from its 1995 consumer business divestment programme. The figure fell slightly short of a forecast range of 808-821 million pounds.
"We had a most solid performance right across the business," Stapleton said.
The company said it planned to pursue an active programme of acquisitions. Stapleton said that Reed Elsevier was interested in acquisitions in professional or business publishing.
He said that the company would like to buy in continental Europe or south-east Asia but said that the most feasible targets remained in north America.

Stapleton said that Reed Elsevier spent over 300 million pounds in 20 transactions last year. He said a big acquisition would be "nice but not necessary", pointing to a 1.6 percent improvement in margins last year.
